question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: one keyless tools/call of microsoft_docs_search, query "Azure Functions durable orchestration", to the endpoint with maxTokenBudget=0, jsonrpc 2.0, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.what-it-answered: HTTP 200, 59003 raw bytes, 28958 content bytes (28958 characters, equal here because this content is pure ASCII), 10 results, content sha256 prefix 2db1a1ad986b7a2f.
decoded.the-vendor-claim-under-test: the vendor README, under Token Budget Control: "To manage token usage and control costs, you can append the maxTokenBudget query parameter to the MCP endpoint URL. This parameter limits the token count in search tool responses by truncating the content to meet your specified budget", marked experimental and "subject to change".
decoded.what-the-two-byte-counts-mean: two byte counts are reported because they measure different things: CONTENT bytes is the UTF-8 length of result.content[0].text, the documentation actually delivered, and RAW is the whole event-stream response. The content sha256 prefix is published so a reader can compare responses across these records without trusting a length. Only bytes were measured; the vendor's claim is about TOKENS and this record does not convert between them.
decoded.the-value-is-ignored-in-silence: 28,958 content bytes and 59,003 raw, with content sha256 prefix 2db1a1ad986b7a2f, which is byte-identical to the unbudgeted response measured in the same pass (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-search-unbudgeted). Not a small response and not an error: the FULL response, to a caller who has asked for a budget of zero. No error, no isError, no warning anywhere in the body.
decoded.why-the-sha-matters-here: identical byte counts would not prove identical content. The sha256 prefixes of the two responses are equal, which is why this record can say byte-identical rather than the same length.
decoded.the-control-is-its-own-record: an unknown TOOL name on this endpoint answers a proper JSON-RPC -32602 (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-unknown-tool-control), so the server has a working error channel and does not use it for this.
decoded.its-sibling: maxTokenBudget=notanumber behaves the same way (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-max-token-budget-unparseable). Zero is parseable and out of range; notanumber is unparseable. Both are ignored.
decoded.not-measured: whether a misspelled PARAMETER NAME behaves the same way. It presumably does, since an unknown query parameter is simply not read, but it was not tried and is not claimed.
decoded.why-this-record-is-one-request: this pull request's records were split so that each is ONE request with one status and one surface, which is what the probe schema's own title says a probe is, after the registry's reviewer held the first head for bundling five different endpoint URLs under one observed.status and one surface. The comparison across budgets lives in the entry's profile and in the decoded fields here, each naming the sibling record it compares with.
decoded.which-reading-this-is: third reading. The five budget requests were sent once at about 12:15Z, again at 12:22:33Z when the raw byte counts were added, and again at 18:06Z as five separately captured requests. Every content and raw figure is identical across all three readings, six hours apart, so the search index behind this query did not move today.

finding: maxTokenBudget=0 is ignored in silence. The keyless query returned 28,958 content bytes and 59,003 raw bytes with content sha256 prefix 2db1a1ad986b7a2f, byte-identical to the unbudgeted response measured in the same pass, carrying no error, no isError and no warning of any kind. A caller who asks this documented cost-control parameter for a budget of zero receives the full response and is told nothing. The control is a separate record: an unknown tool name on this same endpoint draws a proper JSON-RPC -32602, so the error channel exists and is not reached here. This is one of three places on this server where a refusal or an ignored input arrives in the shape of a success.

reproducibility.command: curl -s -X POST 'https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp?maxTokenBudget=0' -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"microsoft_docs_search","arguments":{"query":"Azure Functions durable orchestration"}}}' | sed -n 's/^data: //p' | python3 -c 'import json,sys,hashlib;t=json.load(sys.stdin)["result"]["content"][0]["text"];print(len(t.encode()),len(json.loads(t)["results"]),hashlib.sha256(t.encode()).hexdigest()[:16])'
